     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, write $a = \alpha_0$, and choose and fix
     7	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-gamma-range}
     8	  0 < \gamma < \min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right).
     9	\end{equation}
    10	The interval is nonempty because $\alpha+a < 2$. We use $\langle\xi\rangle =
    11	\sqrt{1+|\xi|^2}$ and set
    12	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-scale-profile}
    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\
    17	    h^{1-\alpha}, & \alpha > 1,
    18	  \end{cases}
    19	  \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    20	\end{equation}

    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.
    46	
    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  If $C = 0$, a countable covering by finite balls gives $\nu = 0$, and the
    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put
    61	  \[
    62	    A_\xi(q) = \int_{|\eta|\le5q}\langle\eta\rangle^{-1}
    63	    \nu_\xi(\ud\eta).
    64	  \]
    65	  Choose $N = \lceil\log_2(5q)\rceil$, so $5q \le 2^N < 10q$. Splitting into the
    66	  unit ball and the annuli $2^j < |\eta| \le 2^{j+1}$ gives
    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and
    72	  is at most $2^{N(\alpha-1)}/(2^{\alpha-1}-1)$ when $\alpha > 1$. Hence,
    73	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}
    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
    81	  with a constant depending only on $\alpha$.
    82	
    83	  Set $q = \max(1,|\xi|)$ and $\epsilon = 1-2\gamma > 0$. On $|\lambda| \le 4q$
    84	  we have $|\eta| \le 5q$. Both bracket powers in $\mathcal{Q}_h$ are at most
    85	  one, since $a-1 < 0$. The contribution of this region to $J_h(\xi)$ is at most
    86	  \[
    87	    2\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q)
    88	    \le 2q^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q).
    89	  \]
    90	  If $\alpha < 1$, this is uniformly bounded
    91	  by~\eqref{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}. If $\alpha = 1$, the bound follows from
    92	  \[
    93	    e^{-\epsilon u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\epsilon},
    94	    \qquad u = \log q \ge 0,
    95	  \]
    96	  since $u e^{-\epsilon u}$ has maximum $1/(e\epsilon)$. If $\alpha > 1$, the
    97	  remaining power is $q^{\alpha+2\gamma-2}$, whose exponent is negative
    98	  by~\eqref{E:variance-gamma-range}. Thus, the near contribution is at most a
    99	  constant times $C$ in all three cases.
   100	
   101	  On the far region write $r = |\lambda| > 4q$. Then
   102	  \[
   103	    |\eta| \ge \frac{3r}4,\qquad
   104	    \big||\eta|-|\xi|\big| \ge \frac r2,\qquad
   105	    |\eta|+|\xi| \ge \frac r2.
   106	  \]
   107	  Each oscillatory bracket is at least $\langle hr\rangle/2$, whereas
   108	  $\langle\eta\rangle^{-1} \le 4/(3r)$ and $\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon} \le
   109	  1$. Consequently, the far contribution is at most
   110	  \[
   111	    \frac43\,2^{2-a}\int_{|\lambda|>4q}
   112	    |\lambda|^{-1}\langle h|\lambda|\rangle^{a-1}\nu(\ud\lambda).
   113	  \]
   114	  Enlarge the domain to $|\lambda| > 1$ and split it into dyadic annuli.
   115	  Applying~\eqref{E:frequency-translated-growth} to their masses bounds this
   116	  expression by a constant depending only on $\alpha,a$ times $C S(h)$, where
   117	  \[
   118	    S(h) = \sum_{j=0}^\infty
   119	    2^{j(\alpha-1)}\langle h2^j\rangle^{a-1}.
   120	  \]
   121	  Choose $L = \lfloor\log_2(1/h)\rfloor \ge 0$. For $j \le L$ the bracket power
   122	  is at most one. For $j \ge L+1$ it is at most $(h2^j)^{a-1}$. Since
   123	  $\alpha+a-2 < 0$, the tail is
   124	  \[
   125	    \frac{h^{a-1}2^{(L+1)(\alpha+a-2)}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}
   126	    \le \frac{h^{1-\alpha}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}.
   127	  \]
   128	  The inequality uses $2^{L+1} > 1/h$ and the negative exponent. The finite sum
   129	  is bounded by $1/(1-2^{\alpha-1})$ for $\alpha < 1$, by $1+\log_2(1/h)$ for
   130	  $\alpha = 1$, and by
   131	  \[
   132	    \frac{2^{\alpha-1}h^{1-\alpha}}{2^{\alpha-1}-1}
   133	  \]
   134	  for $\alpha > 1$. Since $h^{1-\alpha} \le 1$ in the first case, we obtain
   135	  $S(h) \le K_{\alpha,a}B_\alpha(h)$. Combining the near and far bounds, and
   136	  using $B_\alpha(h) \ge 1$, proves the assertion and finiteness of the original
   137	  integral. All constants arose from numerical shell estimates and are
   138	  independent of $d$. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}.
   139	\end{proof}
   140	
   141	\begin{corollary}[A time exponent above one half]\label{C:frequency-time}
   142	  For every
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-beta-range}
   144	    \frac12 < \beta < \min\left(1-\frac a2,
   145	    \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   146	  \end{equation}
   147	  there is a finite $K_\beta = K_\beta(\alpha,a,\gamma,\beta)$ such that
   148	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-time-bound}
   149	    h^{2-a}\sup_\xi J_h(\xi) \le K_\beta C h^{2\beta},
   150	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
   151	  \end{equation}
   152	\end{corollary}
   153	
   154	\begin{proof}
   155	  Both upper endpoints in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range} exceed one half, by $a <
   156	  1$ and $\alpha+a < 2$. If $\alpha < 1$, use $2-a > 2\beta$ in
   157	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}. If $\alpha > 1$, use $3-a-\alpha > 2\beta$.
   158	  For $\alpha = 1$, set $\delta = 2-a-2\beta > 0$ and $u = \log(1/h)$. Then
   159	  \[
   160	    h^\delta(1+\log(1/h))
   161	    = e^{-\delta u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\delta}.
   162	  \]
   163	  This absorbs the critical logarithm. No endpoint value of $\beta$ is used.
   164	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time}.
   165	\end{proof}

   167	\subsection{Forms on the full phase}
   168	
   169	Choose and fix $T > 0$. Set $\Lambda = (1-\Delta)^{1/2}$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
   170	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$. On the complexification of $E = E_s$, use inner
   171	products linear in the first slot. The map
   172	\[
   173	  Jz(\xi) = \left(\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}\widehat{z}_1(\xi),
   174	  \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}\widehat{z}_2(\xi)\right)
   175	\]
   176	is unitary onto $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$. The full massless wave group has
   177	Fourier matrix
   178	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-free-matrix}
   179	  S(t,\xi) =
   180	  \begin{pmatrix}
   181	    \cos(t|\xi|) & \sin(t|\xi|)/|\xi|\\
   182	    -|\xi|\sin(t|\xi|) & \cos(t|\xi|)
   183	  \end{pmatrix},
   184	\end{equation}
   185	where the sine quotient is $t$ at zero. Let $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$. Choose and fix
   186	a real even nonnegative $\zeta \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ equal to one on $B_1$ and
   187	zero off $B_2$, and put $\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$ for $R > 0$. For $I =
   188	[t_0,t_0+h] \subset [0,T]$, $0 < h \le 1$, and Schwartz phases $z,w$, put
   189	\begin{align}
   190	  v_z(t) &= [S(t)z]_1,
   191	  \label{E:variance-displacement}\\
   192	  G_w(t) &= -\frac{\sin(t|D|)}{|D|}\Lambda w_1
   193	  +\cos(t|D|)\Lambda^{-1}w_2,
   194	  \label{E:variance-dual-wave}\\
   195	  F_{z,w}(t,x) &= 1_I(t)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)},
   196	  \qquad \ell_R(I;z,w) = W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF_{z,w}),
   197	  \label{E:variance-actual-form}
   198	\end{align}
   199	where $W_{\mathbb{C}}(F) = W(\operatorname{Re}F)+iW(\operatorname{Im}F)$. There
   200	is no observation cutoff in this definition.
   201	
   202	We first assume $\Gamma \ne 0$. If $\Gamma = 0$, all forms and the column maps
   203	below are zero, so their bounds hold directly. For the nonzero case, let $\nu_R$
   204	be~\eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-measure} and set
   205	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}
   206	  L_\zeta = \|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1,\qquad
   207	  C_\nu = c_d^2L_\zeta^2C_\Gamma.
   208	\end{equation}
   209	Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm} gives a positive even tempered Radon
   210	measure with $\nu_R(B(y,r)) \le C_\nu r^\alpha$, uniformly in $R$.
   211	
   212	\begin{proposition}[Form and phase kernel]\label{P:actual-wave-form}
   213	  The tests $\zeta_RF_{z,w}$ in~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form} belong to the
   214	  original noise completion. The form $\ell_R$ is linear in $z$ and conjugate
   215	  linear in $w$, and uses the same $W$ as the model. For a smooth deterministic
   216	  coefficient $b$ with common compact spatial support and bounded spatial
   217	  derivatives on $[0,T]$,
   218	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-physical-adjoint}
   219	    \langle S(-t)B(b(t))S(t)z,w\rangle_E
   220	    = \int b(t,x)v_z(t,x)\overline{G_w(t,x)}\ud x.
   221	  \end{equation}
   222	  For a real compact smooth $\chi$, multiplication $D_\chi$ on both phase
   223	  entries has adjoint
   224	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}
   225	    D_\chi^{*,E}w
   226	    = \left(\Lambda^{-1}\chi\Lambda w_1,
   227	    \Lambda\chi\Lambda^{-1}w_2\right).
   228	  \end{equation}
   229	  With $U = Jz$, $V = Jw$, $r = |\xi|$, $\rho = |\eta|$ and the continuous
   230	  functions $c_r,b_r$ of Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}, set
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-kernel}
   232	    \mathcal{K}(t;\xi,\eta)
   233	    = \frac1{\sqrt{\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle}}
   234	    \begin{pmatrix}
   235	      -b_rc_\rho & -b_rb_\rho\\
   236	      c_rc_\rho & c_rb_\rho
   237	    \end{pmatrix}(t).
   238	  \end{equation}
   239	  Then
   240	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-normalized-covariance}
   241	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w)|^2
   242	    \le \int\left\|\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2
   243	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   244	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta
   245	    \right\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   246	  \end{equation}
   247	\end{proposition}
   248	
   249	\begin{proof}
   250	  The wave multipliers are smooth at zero through the continuous sine quotient,
   251	  with polynomially bounded frequency derivatives on finite time intervals.
   252	  Bessel multipliers preserve Schwartz space. Thus, $v_z,G_w$ and their product
   253	  are continuous in all Schwartz seminorms on $[0,T]$. For tests supported in a
   254	  fixed compact $K$, the absolute spatial pairing is bounded by
   255	  \[
   256	    |K|\Gamma(K-K)\|F(t)\|_\infty\|H(u)\|_\infty.
   257	  \]
   258	  Indeed, only $y \in K-K$ contributes to $\int\Gamma(\ud y)\int
   259	  F(t,x)\overline{H(u,x-y)}\ud x$. Combine this with the temporal Schur bound
   260	  and approximate the interval indicator and the continuous time dependence by
   261	  smooth interior temporal tests, keeping the spatial support of $\zeta_R$. This
   262	  admits the masked product in the original completion in every allowed
   263	  dimension.
   264	
   265	  We also identify its auxiliary and spectral limits. Approximate a
   266	  Schwartz-valued function on $I$ by time partitions with frozen spatial values,
   267	  and then replace the finitely many indicators by compact smooth temporal
   268	  functions. A diagonal sequence $F_n$ of finite temporal tensors converges in
   269	  $L^2$ time in every Schwartz seminorm. Fourier integration by parts and the
   270	  spatial weighted supremum bounds give, for sufficiently large fixed $N$,

271	  \[
   272	    \|\widehat{F_n-F}(\xi)\|_{L^2(0,T)}
   273	    \le \epsilon_n\langle\xi\rangle^{-N},\qquad \epsilon_n \to 0.
   274	  \]
   275	  Choose $N$ so that the square weight is integrable against both tempered
   276	  measures $\mu$ and $\nu_R$. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} gives
   277	  convergence in their spectral $H_a$ norms. Multiplication by the fixed
   278	  $\zeta_R$ preserves these $L^2$ Schwartz-seminorm limits, so the masked
   279	  differences converge in the $\mu$ spectral norm too. The preceding
   280	  compact-support estimate also gives convergence in the original completion.
   281	  Hence, the auxiliary extension and original-noise limit agree on these
   282	  products. Constants for this admission argument may depend on $R$; they are
   283	  not the uniform variance constants below.
   284	
   285	  For real tensor tests $f,g$, the Hermitian symmetry of their spatial
   286	  transforms gives
   287	  \[
   288	    A(-\xi) = \overline{A(\xi)},\qquad
   289	    A(\xi) = \langle\widehat{f}(\xi),\widehat{g}(\xi)\rangle_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}.
   290	  \]
   291	  Integration against either even $\mu$ or even $\nu_R$ cancels the imaginary
   292	  mixed term. Expanding the squared norm of $\widehat{f}+i\widehat{g}$, then
   293	  using the preceding approximation, extends
   294	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-noise-completion} to the present complex tests:
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-complex-noise}
   296	    \E|W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)|^2
   297	    = (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   298	    \le (2\pi)^d\int\|\widehat{F}(\lambda)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\nu_R(\ud\lambda).
   299	  \end{equation}
   300	  This is a bound for the masked noise, not a declaration that its law is
   301	  stationary. Complex linearity of $W_{\mathbb{C}}$ and linearity of $v_z,G_w$
   302	  prove the stated sesquilinearity.
   303	
   304	  Smooth multiplication is bounded on each Sobolev space: Fourier convolution,
   305	  the inequality $\langle\xi\rangle^r\langle\eta\rangle^{-r} \le
   306	  2^{|r|/2}\langle\xi-\eta\rangle^{|r|}$ and weighted Schwartz decay reduce this
   307	  to the $L^1*L^2$ bound. The free matrix is strongly continuous and bounded on
   308	  $E$ on compact time intervals, directly by its weighted Fourier entries. Thus,
   309	  the ordinary first-response integral exists on states. Since $S(-t)(0,f) =
   310	  (-\sin(t|D|)f/|D|,\cos(t|D|)f)$, moving the real self-adjoint multipliers and
   311	  the two Sobolev weights onto $w$ proves \eqref{E:variance-physical-adjoint}.
   312	  The same weighted duality gives \eqref{E:variance-cutoff-adjoint}. Inserting
   313	  this adjoint in $G_w$ is the correctly observed form; $D_\chi$ need not be
   314	  self-adjoint on $E$. This deterministic identity does not identify a
   315	  positive-width source with the original noise or assert a source limit.
   316	
   317	  The definitions give exactly
   318	  \begin{align*}
   319	    \widehat{v}_z(t,\eta)
   320	    &= \langle\eta\rangle^{-1/2}
   321	    [c_\rho(t)U_1(\eta)+b_\rho(t)U_2(\eta)],\\
   322	    \widehat{G}_w(t,\xi)
   323	    &= \langle\xi\rangle^{-1/2}
   324	    [-b_r(t)V_1(\xi)+c_r(t)V_2(\xi)].
   325	  \end{align*}
   326	  Their product gives~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel}. At zero frequencies
   327	  one uses the continuous sine quotient, not division by zero; at $\xi = \eta =
   328	  0$ the matrix is
   329	  $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-t&-t^2\\1&t\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Fourier
   330	  multiplication with the conjugate yields
   331	  \[
   332	    \widehat{F}_{z,w}(t,-\lambda)
   333	    = c_d1_I(t)\int\sum_{i,j=1}^2\mathcal{K}_{ij}(t;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   334	    U_j(\eta)\overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}\ud\eta.
   335	  \]
   336	  The spatial integral is absolutely convergent uniformly on the finite time
   337	  interval by Schwartz decay. The Schur bound also makes it a Bochner
   338	  $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ integral. Reflect $\lambda$ using evenness of $\nu_R$
   339	  in~\eqref{E:variance-complex-noise}. Since $(2\pi)^dc_d^2 = 1$, this
   340	  proves~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} with no remaining Fourier
   341	  factor. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}.
   342	\end{proof}

   344	\subsection{Bessel's inequality and the two variances}
   345	
   346	\begin{lemma}[Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality]\label{L:phase-bessel}
   347	  Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $\{u_k\}$ be a finite
   348	  orthonormal family in $L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2)$, and let $g = (g_1,g_2) \in
   349	  L^2(\R^d;H^2)$. Then
   350	  \begin{equation}\label{E:phase-bessel}
   351	    \sum_k\left\|\int\sum_{j=1}^2u_{k,j}(\eta)g_j(\eta)\ud\eta\right\|_H^2
   352	    \le \int\sum_{j=1}^2\|g_j(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   353	  \end{equation}
   354	  The same bound holds with $\overline{u_{k,j}}$ in place of $u_{k,j}$.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	
   357	\begin{proof}
   358	  Expand $g$ in a countable orthonormal basis of $H$. On each scalar coefficient
   359	  apply scalar Bessel to the orthonormal family $\{\overline{u_k}\}$, or to
   360	  $\{u_k\}$ for the conjugated version. Scalar finite Bessel follows by
   361	  subtracting an orthogonal finite projection and expanding its nonnegative
   362	  squared norm. Sum over the $H$ basis and use Parseval and nonnegative Tonelli.
   363	  The Bochner integrals exist by $L^2$ Cauchy--Schwarz. A finite-dimensional $H$
   364	  uses its finite basis, and the zero space is immediate. No independence is
   365	  involved. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}.
   366	\end{proof}
   367	
   368	\begin{proposition}[Both variance directions]\label{P:wave-two-variances}
   369	  There is a finite $C_T$, depending on the fixed model, mask,
   370	  $a,\alpha,\gamma,T$, but not on $R,I$ or the orthonormal family, such that for
   371	  every finite complex $E$-orthonormal Schwartz family $\{e_k\}$ and every
   372	  Schwartz phase $z$,
   373	  \begin{align}
   374	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;e_k,z)|^2
   375	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2,
   376	    \label{E:wave-input-variance}\\
   377	    \sum_k\E|\ell_R(I;z,e_k)|^2
   378	    &\le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2.
   379	    \label{E:wave-output-variance}
   380	  \end{align}
   381	  For every $\beta$ in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range}, either right side may be
   382	  replaced by $C_{T,\beta}h^{2\beta}\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2$.
   383	\end{proposition}
   384	
   385	\begin{proof}
   386	  Each entry in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-kernel} is a product of two
   387	  continuous wave factors times $(\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle)^{-1/2}$,
   388	  with a possible minus sign. Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave} therefore
   389	  gives
   390	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-kernel-time-bound}
   391	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   392	    \le A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\xi,\eta),
   393	    \qquad A_T = C_1(a)(1+T)^4.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	  The positive even Radon measure $\nu_R$ satisfies the growth bound
   396	  \eqref{E:variance-actual-growth-constant}. Thus, all hypotheses of
   397	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row} hold, and
   398	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-actual-row-bound}
   399	    \int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)
   400	    \le K C_\nu B_\alpha(h)\langle\xi\rangle^{-2\gamma}.
   401	  \end{equation}
   402	  No nonnegative physical inverse covariance of $\nu_R$ is needed.
   403	
   404	  The kernels used in Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} belong to its stated $L^2$
   405	  space for each fixed $\lambda$. Indeed, $|c_r(t)| \le 1$ and $|b_r(t)| \le
   406	  \sqrt{2}\max(1,T)$ on $[0,T]$, by the high- and low-frequency representations.
   407	  The kernels are continuous into $L^2(0,T)$ in their frequency variables, hence
   408	  into $H_a^{\mathbb{C}}$ by Schur. Separability gives strong measurability.
   409	  Multiplication by shifted Schwartz components of $U$ or $V$ then gives the
   410	  required $L^2$ integrability. Later $\lambda$ integrals are of nonnegative
   411	  functions; their finiteness follows from the estimates below.
   412	
   413	  First fix $V = Jz$ and let $U_k = Je_k$ be the input family.
   414	  In~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance} set
   415	  \[
   416	    g_j^\lambda(\eta) = \sum_{i=1}^2
   417	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   418	    \overline{V_i(\eta+\lambda)}.
   419	  \]
   420	  Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel} and Cauchy--Schwarz over the two output components
   421	  give
   422	  \begin{align*}
   423	    \sum_j\|g_j^\lambda(\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2
   424	    &\le 2\sum_{i,j}|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2
   425	    \|1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\eta+\lambda,\eta)\|_{H_a^{\mathbb{C}}}^2\\
   426	    &\le 4A_T h^{2-a}\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)
   427	    \sum_i|V_i(\eta+\lambda)|^2.
   428	  \end{align*}
   429	  Change variables $\xi = \eta+\lambda$ in the Lebesgue integral for each
   430	  $\lambda$, apply Tonelli and~\eqref{E:variance-actual-row-bound}, and use
   431	  $\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}} = \|\langle\xi\rangle^{-\gamma}Jz\|_2$. This
   432	  proves~\eqref{E:wave-input-variance} with $C_T = 4A_TKC_\nu$.

   434	  Next fix $U = Jz$ and let $V_k = Je_k$ be the output family. After $\eta =
   435	  \xi-\lambda$ in~\eqref{E:variance-normalized-covariance}, put
   436	  \[
   437	    f_i^\lambda(\xi) = \sum_{j=1}^2
   438	    1_I\mathcal{K}_{ij}(\cdot;\xi,\xi-\lambda)U_j(\xi-\lambda).
   439	  \]
   440	  Apply the conjugated version of Lemma~\ref{L:phase-bessel}. Cauchy--Schwarz
   441	  over the two input components bounds its right side by
   442	  \[
   443	    4A_T h^{2-a}\int\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)
   444	    \sum_j|U_j(\xi-\lambda)|^2\ud\xi.
   445	  \]

   447	  $\int\Phi_h(\eta+\lambda,\eta)\nu_R(\ud\lambda)$. Reflect $\lambda$ using the

   457	  used as this uniform variance bound. This proves
   458	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}.

   461	\subsection{Mean-square columns on the original probability space}
   462	
   463	Write $E_r^{\mathrm{real}}$ for the real phase space in dimension $d$.
   464	
   465	\begin{proposition}[Column and adjoint-column maps]\label{P:wave-square-columns}
   466	  On the same probability space there are deterministic bounded real linear maps
   467	  \[
   468	    m_{R,I},n_{R,I}:E_{s-\gamma}^{\mathrm{real}}\longrightarrow
   469	    L^2(\Omega;E_s^{\mathrm{real}}),
   470	  \]
   471	  with squared bounds $C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)$, such that, for every fixed real
   472	  Schwartz pair $z,w$,
   473	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-square-columns}
   474	    \langle m_{R,I}z,w\rangle_E
   475	    = \ell_R(I;z,w) = \langle z,n_{R,I}w\rangle_E
   476	    \quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
   477	  \end{equation}
   478	  Fixed-vector values and finite families of values are centered Gaussian.
   479	\end{proposition}
   480	
   481	\begin{proof}
   482	  Choose a countable real Schwartz orthonormal basis $\{e_k\}$ of $E_s$. Such a
   483	  basis follows by Gram--Schmidt from a countable dense Schwartz family,
   484	  discarding zero residuals. Schwartz density follows by smooth Fourier cutoff
   485	  approximation in the weighted $L^2$ norms: approximate by compact smooth
   486	  Fourier coordinates, replace $g(\xi)$ by $(g(\xi)+\overline{g(-\xi)})/2$, and
   487	  apply the inverse Bessel/Fourier maps. The resulting phases are real Schwartz,
   488	  and Gram--Schmidt preserves that class. The same density holds in
   489	  $E_{s-\gamma}$.
   490	
   491	  For fixed real Schwartz $z$, define
   492	  \[
   493	    m_N(z) = \sum_{k\le N}\ell_R(I;z,e_k)e_k,
   494	    \qquad n_N(z) = \sum_{k\le N}\ell_R(I;e_k,z)e_k.
   495	  \]
   496	  Both are finite Gaussian sums on the original $W$. By
   497	  Proposition~\ref{P:wave-two-variances}, their coefficient expected squares
   498	  have finite sum. Orthogonality gives the squared tail norms as the
   499	  corresponding sums of expected squares. Thus, both sequences converge in
   500	  $L^2(\Omega;E_s)$ to $m(z),n(z)$ with the asserted bounds, without
   501	  independence of the coefficients. Finite-sum measurability and separable $E_s$
   502	  give strong measurability of the limits. The bounded real linear maps extend
   503	  uniquely from Schwartz phases to $E_{s-\gamma}$.
   504	
   505	  If $w_N$ is the $E_s$ projection of a Schwartz $w$ onto the first $N$ basis
   506	  vectors, then $\langle m_N(z),w\rangle_E = \ell_R(I;z,w_N)$. The singleton
   507	  form of~\eqref{E:wave-output-variance}, after normalizing $w-w_N$ in $E_s$,
   508	  gives
   509	  \[
   510	    \E|\ell_R(I;z,w-w_N)|^2
   511	    \le C_T h^{2-a}B_\alpha(h)\|z\|_{E_{s-\gamma}}^2\|w-w_N\|_{E_s}^2.
   512	  \]
   513	  The zero residual is immediate. The right side tends to zero, giving the first
   514	  identity in~\eqref{E:variance-square-columns}. For the second, project $z$
   515	  instead and use the singleton input bound \eqref{E:wave-input-variance}. A
   516	  fixed countable Schwartz orthonormal basis and Parseval show basis
   517	  independence of the constructed limits.
   518	
   519	  Continuous linear functionals of the limits, and finite linear combinations of
   520	  such functionals, are $L^2$ limits of centered Gaussian variables with
   521	  convergent variances. Their characteristic functions therefore converge to
   522	  those of centered Gaussians. The same reasoning after the bounded input
   523	  extension proves joint Gaussianity for arbitrary fixed inputs and finite
   524	  families of the two maps. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:wave-square-columns}.
   525	\end{proof}
   526	
   527	These are maps into $L^2(\Omega;E_s)$ for fixed intervals. No common uncountable
   528	almost-sure version, random bounded operator, Hilbert--Schmidt realization, time
   529	path, source convergence or new solution-moment bound is inferred by this
   530	section alone. Both variance directions are retained in
   531	Section~\ref{S:actual-operator-driver}.

   156	    (c : ℕ → ENNReal) (h0 : ‖x - y‖ ≤ 1 → F ≤ c 0)
   157	    (hs : ∀ n : ℕ, (2 : ℝ) ^ n ≤ ‖x - y‖ → ‖x - y‖ ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) → F ≤ c (n + 1)) :
   158	    F ≤ ∑' j, (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)).indicator (fun _ => c j) x := by
   159	  by_cases h1 : ‖x - y‖ ≤ 1
   160	  · refine le_trans ?_ (ENNReal.le_tsum 0)
   161	    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem (by simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm] using h1)]
   162	    exact h0 h1
   163	  · replace h1 := not_le.mp h1
   164	    obtain ⟨n, hn1, hn2⟩ := exists_nat_pow_near h1.le (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 2)
   165	    refine le_trans ?_ (ENNReal.le_tsum (n + 1))
   166	    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem (by simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm] using hn2.le)]

   170	normed group with its Borel σ-algebra. -/
   171	theorem lintegral_shellSum {E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E]

   173	    ∫⁻ x, ∑' j, (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)).indicator (fun _ => c j) x ∂ν =
   174	      ∑' j, c j * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)) := by
   175	  rw [lintegral_tsum fun j => (measurable_const.indicator measurableSet_closedBall).aemeasurable]

   179	/-- The open-ball growth bound gives the closed-ball bound (TeX l. 29-31: apply it at
   180	radius `r + ε` and let `ε ↓ 0`). Any measure on a pseudometric space. -/
   181	theorem closedBall_le {E : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] (ν : Measure E)
   182	    {C α : ℝ} (hgrowth : ∀ y : E, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ν (ball y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ α))
   183	    (y : E) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
   184	    ν (closedBall y R) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * R ^ α) := by
   185	  have hT : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (C * (R + ε) ^ α)) (𝓝[>] 0)
   186	      (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal (C * R ^ α))) := by
   187	    apply ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal
   188	    apply Tendsto.mono_left _ nhdsWithin_le_nhds
   189	    have : Continuous fun ε : ℝ => R + ε := by fun_prop
   190	    have hc : ContinuousAt (fun ε : ℝ => C * (R + ε) ^ α) 0 := by
   191	      apply ContinuousAt.mul continuousAt_const
   192	      apply ContinuousAt.rpow_const this.continuousAt
   193	      left; simp [hR.ne']
   194	    simpa using hc.tendsto
   195	  apply ge_of_tendsto hT
   196	  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with ε hε
   197	  calc ν (closedBall y R) ≤ ν (ball y (R + ε)) :=
   198	        measure_mono (closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith [show (0:ℝ) < ε from hε]))
   199	    _ ≤ _ := hgrowth y _ (by linarith [show (0:ℝ) < ε from hε])
   200	
   201	/-- Shell sum bounded by the growth constant (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   202	theorem shellSum_le {E : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] (ν : Measure E)
   203	    {C α : ℝ}
   204	    (hgrowth : ∀ y : E, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ν (ball y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ α))
   205	    (y : E) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j) :
   206	    ∑' j, ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)) ≤
   207	      ∑' j, ENNReal.ofReal (c j * C * ((2 : ℝ) ^ α) ^ j) := by
   208	  apply ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum; intro j
   209	  calc ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j))
   210	      ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ENNReal.ofReal (C * ((2 : ℝ) ^ j) ^ α) :=
   211	        by gcongr; exact closedBall_le ν hgrowth y (by positivity)

   217	/-- The scale profile `B_α(h)` of `E:variance-scale-profile` (TeX l. 12-19):
   218	`1` for `α < 1`, `1 + log(1/h)` for `α = 1`, `h^{1-α}` for `α > 1`. -/
   219	def scaleProfile (α h : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   220	  if α < 1 then 1 else if α = 1 then 1 + Real.log (1 / h) else h ^ (1 - α)

   224	    1 ≤ scaleProfile α h := by
   225	  unfold scaleProfile
   226	  split_ifs with hα hα'
   227	  · exact le_rfl
   228	  · have : 0 ≤ Real.log (1 / h) := Real.log_nonneg (by rw [le_div_iff₀ h0]; linarith)
   229	    linarith
   230	  · exact Real.one_le_rpow_of_pos_of_le_one_of_nonpos h0 h1 (by
   231	      rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hα' with h' | h' <;> [exact absurd h' hα; linarith])

   235	  ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α - 1)) ^ n * bracket (h * 2 ^ n) ^ (a - 1)

   237	/-- Terms of `S(h)` are nonnegative (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/

   239	  mul_nonneg (by positivity) (bracket_rpow_nonneg _ _)

   241	/-- Head majorant of a term (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/

   243	    rowSeries α a h n ≤ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α - 1)) ^ n := by
   244	  unfold rowSeries
   245	  have := bracket_rpow_le_one ha (h * 2 ^ n)
   246	  have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α - 1)) ^ n := by positivity
   247	  nlinarith

   249	/-- Tail majorant of a term (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   250	theorem rowSeries_le_tail {α a h : ℝ} (ha : a < 1) (h0 : 0 < h) (n : ℕ) :
   251	    rowSeries α a h n ≤ h ^ (a - 1) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α + a - 2)) ^ n := by
   252	  unfold rowSeries
   253	  have hx : 0 < h * 2 ^ n := by positivity
   254	  have h1 : bracket (h * 2 ^ n) ^ (a - 1) ≤ (h * 2 ^ n) ^ (a - 1) :=
   255	    Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos hx
   256	      (by simpa [abs_of_pos hx] using abs_le_bracket (h * 2 ^ n)) (by linarith)
   257	  have h2 : (h * 2 ^ n) ^ (a - 1) = h ^ (a - 1) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ (a - 1)) ^ n := by
   258	    rw [Real.mul_rpow h0.le (by positivity), two_pow_rpow]
   259	  have h3 : ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α + a - 2)) ^ n = ((2 : ℝ) ^ (α - 1)) ^ n * ((2 : ℝ) ^ (a - 1)) ^ n := by
   260	    rw [← mul_pow, ← Real.rpow_add (by norm_num)]; ring_nf
   261	  rw [h3]

   264	    _ = _ := by rw [h2]; ring

   266	/-- `2^s < 1` for `s < 0` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/

   268	  Real.rpow_lt_one_of_one_lt_of_neg (by norm_num) hs

   276	/-- The estimate `S(h) ≤ K_{α,a} B_α(h)` (TeX l. 120-133), with `K` independent of `h`. -/

   391	/-! ### The kernel, the row integral and pointwise bounds -/
   392	
   393	/-- The kernel `Φ_h(ξ,η) = 𝒬_h(|ξ|,|η|)/(⟨ξ⟩⟨η⟩)` of `E:frequency-row-kernel` (TeX l. 33-37),
   394	with `𝒬_h = frequencyPair` of `E:masked-frequency-pair`. -/
   395	def rowKernel {d : ℕ} (a h : ℝ) (ξ η : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   396	  frequencyPair a h ‖ξ‖ ‖η‖ / (bracket ‖ξ‖ * bracket ‖η‖)
   397	
   398	/-- The row integral `J_h(ξ) = ⟨ξ⟩^{2γ} ∫ Φ_h(ξ, ξ-λ) ν(dλ)` of `E:frequency-row-integral`
   399	(TeX l. 38-41), as a nonnegative extended integral (TeX l. 42). -/
   400	def rowIntegral {d : ℕ} (a γ h : ℝ) (ν : Measure (Rd d)) (ξ : Rd d) : ENNReal :=
   401	  ENNReal.ofReal (bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ)) * ∫⁻ l, ENNReal.ofReal (rowKernel a h ξ (ξ - l)) ∂ν
   402	
   403	/-- `Φ_h ≥ 0`. -/
   404	theorem rowKernel_nonneg {d : ℕ} (a h : ℝ) (ξ η : Rd d) : 0 ≤ rowKernel a h ξ η :=
   405	  div_nonneg (frequencyPair_nonneg _ _ _ _)
   406	    (mul_nonneg (bracket_pos _).le (bracket_pos _).le)
   407	
   408	/-- `λ ↦ Φ_h(ξ, ξ-λ)` is continuous, hence Borel measurable (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   409	theorem continuous_rowKernel {d : ℕ} (a h : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) :
   410	    Continuous fun l : Rd d => rowKernel a h ξ (ξ - l) := by
   411	  unfold rowKernel frequencyPair
   412	  have hb : ∀ f : Rd d → ℝ, Continuous f → ∀ e : ℝ, Continuous fun l => bracket (f l) ^ e :=
   413	    fun f hf e => (continuous_bracket.comp hf).rpow_const fun l => Or.inl (bracket_pos _).ne'
   414	  refine Continuous.div ?_ ?_ fun l => (mul_pos (bracket_pos _) (bracket_pos _)).ne'
   415	  · exact (hb _ (by fun_prop) _).add (hb _ (by fun_prop) _)
   416	  · exact continuous_const.mul (continuous_bracket.comp (by fun_prop))
   417	
   418	/-- The weighted kernel equals `⟨ξ⟩^{2γ-1} 𝒬_h / ⟨η⟩` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   419	theorem weighted_eq {d : ℕ} (a γ h : ℝ) (ξ η : Rd d) :
   420	    bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ) * rowKernel a h ξ η =
   421	      bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ - 1) * frequencyPair a h ‖ξ‖ ‖η‖ / bracket ‖η‖ := by
   422	  unfold rowKernel
   423	  rw [Real.rpow_sub_one (bracket_pos _).ne']
   424	  have := (bracket_pos ‖ξ‖).ne'; have := (bracket_pos ‖η‖).ne'
   425	  field_simp

   427	/-- Global bound `⟨ξ⟩^{2γ}Φ_h ≤ 2` for `a < 1`, `2γ ≤ 1` (auxiliary to the Lean proof route). -/
   428	theorem weighted_le_two {d : ℕ} {a γ : ℝ} (ha : a < 1) (hγ : 2 * γ ≤ 1) (h : ℝ) (ξ η : Rd d) :
   429	    bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ) * rowKernel a h ξ η ≤ 2 := by
   430	  rw [weighted_eq]
   431	  have h1 : bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ - 1) ≤ 1 :=
   432	    Real.rpow_le_one_of_one_le_of_nonpos (one_le_bracket _) (by linarith)
   433	  have h2 := frequencyPair_le_two ha h ‖ξ‖ ‖η‖
   434	  have h3 := frequencyPair_nonneg a h ‖ξ‖ ‖η‖
   435	  have h4 : 0 ≤ bracket ‖ξ‖ ^ (2 * γ - 1) := bracket_rpow_nonneg _ _
   436	  rw [div_le_iff₀ (bracket_pos _)]
   437	  have := one_le_bracket ‖η‖
   438	  nlinarith [mul_le_mul h1 h2 h3 zero_le_one]
   439	
   440	/-- Near-region shell bound (replaces the three-case bound of TeX l. 60-99): if `‖λ‖ ≤ 4‖ξ‖` and
   441	`2^n ≤ ‖ξ - λ‖`, then `⟨ξ⟩^{2γ}Φ_h(ξ,ξ-λ) ≤ 2 (2^n/5)^{2γ-1} 2^{-n}` (auxiliary). -/
   442	theorem weighted_le_near {d : ℕ} {a γ : ℝ} (ha : a < 1) (hγ : 2 * γ ≤ 1) (h : ℝ) (ξ l : Rd d)

  7977	  summary: "InputBound p s h nu gamma M: for every L^2-orthonormal U_k (k<n) and V in L^2: all eta-integrands integrable, <xi>^(-2gamma) sum|V_i|^2 integrable, sum_k int^- ||coef U_k V l||^2 nu(dl) <= M int <xi>^(-2gamma) sum_i |V_i|^2."
  7978	  keywords: [input-direction, spectral-form]
  7979	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  7980	  status: reusable
  7981	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-output-bound
  7982	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.OutputBound
  7983	  kind: definition
  7984	  summary: "OutputBound p s h nu gamma M: for U in L^2 and every L^2-orthonormal V_k (k<n): all eta-integrands integrable, <xi>^(-2gamma) sum|U_j|^2 integrable, sum_k int^- ||coef U V_k l||^2 nu(dl) <= M int <xi>^(-2gamma) sum_j |U_j|^2."
  7985	  keywords: [output-direction, spectral-form]
  7986	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  7987	  status: reusable
  7988	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-wave-two-variances
  7989	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.wave_two_variances
  7990	  kind: theorem
  7991	  summary: "If a<1, alpha+a<2, gamma>=0, 2gamma<=1, alpha+2gamma<2: exists K>=0, for all p (p.a=a), d, nu with nu(B(y,r))<=C r^alpha (C>=0), [s,s+h] in [0,T], 0<h<=1: InputBound with M=4 A_T K C h^(2-a) B_alpha(h); OutputBound too if nu even."
  7992	  keywords: [wave-variance, spectral-core]
  7993	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  7994	  status: reusable
  7995	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-input-bound-mono
  7996	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.InputBound.mono
  7997	  kind: theorem
  7998	  summary: "If M <= M' then InputBound p s h nu gamma M implies InputBound p s h nu gamma M'."
  7999	  keywords: [input-direction, monotonicity]
  8000	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8001	  status: internal
  8002	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-output-bound-mono
  8003	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.OutputBound.mono
  8004	  kind: theorem
  8005	  summary: "If M <= M' then OutputBound p s h nu gamma M implies OutputBound p s h nu gamma M'."
  8006	  keywords: [output-direction, monotonicity]
  8007	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8008	  status: internal
  8009	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-wave-two-variances-beta
  8010	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.wave_two_variances_beta
  8011	  kind: theorem
  8012	  summary: "Hypotheses of wave_two_variances plus 2beta < 2-a and 2beta < 3-a-alpha: exists Kbeta>=0 such that, for the same p, d, nu, C, s, h, InputBound holds with M = 4 A_T Kbeta C h^(2beta), and OutputBound too if nu is even."
  8013	  keywords: [wave-variance, time-exponent]
  8014	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8015	  status: reusable
  8016	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-cnu
  8017	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.Cnu
  8018	  kind: definition
  8019	  summary: "Cnu Gamma zeta = c_d^2 * Lz(zeta)^2 * C_Gamma, with Lz = MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.Lz (the L^1 norm of zeta-hat) and C_Gamma = MaskedSpectralGrowth.CGamma Gamma: the constant C_nu."
  8020	  keywords: [growth-constant, auxiliary-measure]
  8021	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8022	  status: reusable
  8023	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-cnu-nonneg
  8024	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.Cnu_nonneg
  8025	  kind: theorem
  8026	  summary: "For every Gamma and zeta: 0 <= Cnu Gamma zeta."
  8027	  keywords: [growth-constant, nonnegativity]
  8028	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8029	  status: internal
  8030	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-nu-growth
  8031	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.nu_growth
  8032	  kind: theorem
  8033	  summary: "Under HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu, for real Schwartz zeta, R > 0, y in R^d, r > 0: nu_R(B(y, r)) <= Cnu Gamma zeta * r^alpha (nu_R = MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.nu mu zeta R, open ball)."
  8034	  keywords: [auxiliary-measure, ball-growth]
  8035	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8036	  status: reusable
  8037	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-wave-two-variances-core-paper
  8038	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.wave_two_variances_core_paper
  8039	  kind: theorem
  8040	  summary: "Under H:homog, 0<gamma<min(1/2,(2-alpha)/2), p.a=alpha0, mask zeta (even, >=0, 1 on B_1, 0 off B_2): exists K>=0, for R>0, [t0,t0+h] in [0,T], 0<h<=1, Input/OutputBound for nu_R with M=4 A_T K C_nu h^(2-alpha0) B_alpha(h)."
  8041	  keywords: [wave-variance, auxiliary-measure]
  8042	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8043	  status: reusable
  8044	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-wave-two-variances-core-beta-paper
  8045	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.wave_two_variances_core_beta_paper
  8046	  kind: theorem
  8047	  summary: "Hypotheses of wave_two_variances_core_paper plus 1/2 < beta < min(1-alpha0/2, (3-alpha0-alpha)/2): exists Kbeta>=0 such that Input/OutputBound hold for nu_R with M = 4 A_T Kbeta C_nu h^(2beta), for all R > 0 and admissible t0, h."
  8048	  keywords: [wave-variance, time-exponent]
  8049	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8050	  status: reusable
  8051	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-sum-le-of-of-real
  8052	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.sum_le_of_ofReal
  8053	  kind: theorem
  8054	  summary: "For x : Fin n -> R and A >= 0: if sum_k ofReal(x k) <= ofReal A then sum_k x k <= A."
  8055	  keywords: [ennreal, real-transfer]
  8056	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8057	  status: internal
  8058	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-orthonormal-j
  8059	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.orthonormal_J
  8060	  kind: theorem
  8061	  summary: "If J : P -> (Fin 2 -> R^d -> C) has L^2 components and int sum_j (J z)_j conj((J w)_j) = inner w z, then an orthonormal e : Fin n -> P gives IsOrthonormalL2 volume (k |-> J (e k))."
  8062	  keywords: [orthonormal-family, isometry]
  8063	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8064	  status: internal
  8065	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/wave-two-variances-wave-two-variances-paper
  8066	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.WaveTwoVariances.wave_two_variances_paper
  8067	  kind: theorem
  8068	  summary: "Hypotheses of the core wrapper; J isometric into L^2 (hJL2, hJ); normSG z^2 = int <xi>^(-2gamma) sum|Jz_i|^2; hlink: ofReal var(z,w) <= int^- ||coef(Jz,Jw)||^2 dnu_R. Then sum_k var(e_k,z), sum_k var(z,e_k) <= C_T h^(2-a) B normSG z^2 and the h^(2beta) form."
  8069	  keywords: [wave-variance, named-inputs]
  8070	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveTwoVariances.lean
  8071	  status: reusable

  4617	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-row-paper
  4618	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequency_row_paper
  4619	  kind: theorem
  4620	  summary: "With the section's hypotheses (H:homog with a = alpha0, 0 < gamma < min(1/2,(2-alpha)/2)), there is K >= 0 such that for all d, Gamma, mu, locally finite nu, C >= 0 with nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha for all y and r > 0, 0 < h <= 1: sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h), with integrability."
  4621	  keywords: [frequency-row, dyadic-shell]
  4622	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4623	  status: reusable
  4624	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-row
  4625	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequency_row
  4626	  kind: theorem
  4627	  summary: "If a < 1, alpha + a < 2, 2 gamma <= 1, alpha + 2 gamma < 2: exists K >= 0, forall d, nu on R^d, C >= 0 with nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha for all y and r > 0 (open balls), 0 < h <= 1: sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h); each row kernel is nu-integrable with the same real bound."
  4628	  keywords: [frequency-row, dyadic-shell]
  4629	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4630	  status: reusable
  4631	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-integral-le
  4632	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowIntegral_le
  4633	  kind: theorem
  4634	  summary: "If a < 1, alpha + a < 2, 2 gamma <= 1, alpha + 2 gamma < 2: exists K >= 0, forall d, nu on R^d, C >= 0 with nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha for all y and r > 0 (open balls), 0 < h <= 1, xi: J_h(xi) <= ofReal(K C B_alpha(h)) (pointwise form)."
  4635	  keywords: [frequency-row, dyadic-shell]
  4636	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4637	  status: reusable
  4638	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-time-paper
  4639	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequency_time_paper
  4640	  kind: theorem
  4641	  summary: "With the section's hypotheses (0 < gamma < min(1/2,(2-alpha)/2)) and 1/2 < beta < min(1-a/2,(3-a-alpha)/2): exists K_beta >= 0, forall d, Gamma, mu with H:homog (a = alpha0), locally finite nu, C >= 0 with growth, 0 < h <= 1: h^(2-a) sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K_beta C h^(2 beta)."
  4642	  keywords: [frequency-time, time-exponent]
  4643	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4644	  status: reusable
  4645	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-time
  4646	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequency_time
  4647	  kind: theorem
  4648	  summary: "If a < 1, alpha + a < 2, 2 gamma <= 1, alpha + 2 gamma < 2, 2 beta < 2 - a, 2 beta < 3 - a - alpha: exists K_beta >= 0, forall d, nu, C >= 0 with nu(B(y,r)) <= C r^alpha for all y and r > 0 (open balls), 0 < h <= 1: h^(2-a) sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K_beta C h^(2 beta)."
  4649	  keywords: [frequency-time, time-exponent]
  4650	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4651	  status: reusable
  4652	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-scale-time-le
  4653	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.scale_time_le
  4654	  kind: theorem
  4655	  summary: "For real alpha, a, beta with 2 beta < 2 - a and 2 beta < 3 - a - alpha: exists c >= 0 such that h^(2-a) B_alpha(h) <= c h^(2 beta) for all 0 < h <= 1 (absorbs the log at alpha = 1)."
  4656	  keywords: [frequency-time, scale-profile]
  4657	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4658	  status: reusable
  4659	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-series-tsum-le
  4660	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowSeries_tsum_le
  4661	  kind: theorem
  4662	  summary: "If a < 1 and alpha + a < 2: exists K >= 0 such that for all 0 < h <= 1, sum_j 2^(j(alpha-1)) <h 2^j>^(a-1) <= K B_alpha(h)."
  4663	  keywords: [dyadic-series, scale-profile]
  4664	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4665	  status: reusable
  4666	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-summable-row-series
  4667	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.summable_rowSeries
  4668	  kind: theorem
  4669	  summary: "If a < 1, alpha + a < 2 and h > 0, the series n -> 2^(n(alpha-1)) <h 2^n>^(a-1) is summable."
  4670	  keywords: [dyadic-series, summability]
  4671	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4672	  status: reusable
  4673	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-closed-ball-le
  4674	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.closedBall_le
  4675	  kind: theorem
  4676	  summary: "For a measure nu on a pseudometric space with nu(ball y r) <= ofReal(C r^alpha) for all y and r > 0: nu(closedBall y R) <= ofReal(C R^alpha) for every y and R > 0."
  4677	  keywords: [growth-bound, closed-ball]
  4678	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4679	  status: reusable
  4680	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-one-le-scale-profile
  4681	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.one_le_scaleProfile
  4682	  kind: theorem
  4683	  summary: "For real alpha and 0 < h <= 1: 1 <= B_alpha(h)."
  4684	  keywords: [scale-profile, lower-bound]
  4685	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4686	  status: reusable
  4687	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-pair-le-two
  4688	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequencyPair_le_two
  4689	  kind: theorem
  4690	  summary: "If a < 1, then Q_h(r,rho) = <h(r-rho)>^(a-1) + <h(r+rho)>^(a-1) <= 2 for all real h, r, rho."
  4691	  keywords: [frequency-pair, upper-bound]
  4692	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4693	  status: reusable
  4694	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-bracket-rpow-le-half
  4695	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.bracket_rpow_le_half
  4696	  kind: theorem
  4697	  summary: "If a < 1, t >= 0 and t/2 <= |x|, then <x>^(a-1) <= 2^(1-a) <t>^(a-1)."
  4698	  keywords: [japanese-bracket, rpow-bound]
  4699	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4700	  status: reusable
  4701	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-scale-profile
  4702	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.scaleProfile
  4703	  kind: definition
  4704	  summary: "B_alpha(h): 1 if alpha < 1, 1 + log(1/h) if alpha = 1, h^(1-alpha) if alpha > 1 (defined for all real h; the manuscript uses 0 < h <= 1)."
  4705	  keywords: [scale-profile, definition]
  4706	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4707	  status: reusable
  4708	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-kernel
  4709	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowKernel
  4710	  kind: definition
  4711	  summary: "Phi_h(xi,eta) = Q_h(|xi|,|eta|) / (<|xi|> <|eta|>) on R^d, with Q_h = MaskedTrigProducts.frequencyPair a h."
  4712	  keywords: [frequency-row, kernel]
  4713	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4714	  status: reusable
  4715	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-integral
  4716	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowIntegral
  4717	  kind: definition
  4718	  summary: "J_h(xi) = ofReal(<xi>^(2 gamma)) * lintegral of ofReal(Phi_h(xi, xi - lambda)) d nu(lambda), a nonnegative extended (ENNReal) integral."
  4719	  keywords: [frequency-row, lower-integral]
  4720	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4721	  status: reusable
  4722	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-series
  4723	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowSeries
  4724	  kind: definition
  4725	  summary: "Term n of S(h): 2^(n(alpha-1)) * <h 2^n>^(a-1), written ((2:R)^(alpha-1))^n * bracket(h * 2^n)^(a-1)."
  4726	  keywords: [dyadic-series, definition]
  4727	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4728	  status: reusable
  4729	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-one-le-bracket
  4730	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.one_le_bracket
  4731	  kind: theorem

  4735	  status: internal

  4743	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-abs-le-bracket
  4744	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.abs_le_bracket

  4748	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4749	  status: internal
  4750	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-bracket-mono
  4751	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.bracket_mono
  4752	  kind: theorem
  4753	  summary: "If |x| <= |y| then <x> <= <y>."

  4757	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-continuous-bracket
  4758	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.continuous_bracket
  4759	  kind: theorem
  4760	  summary: "The bracket x -> sqrt(1 + x^2) is continuous on R."

  4763	  status: internal
  4764	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-bracket-rpow-le-one
  4765	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.bracket_rpow_le_one
  4766	  kind: theorem

  4769	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean

  4771	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-bracket-rpow-nonneg
  4772	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.bracket_rpow_nonneg

  4776	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean

  4778	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-frequency-pair-nonneg
  4779	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.frequencyPair_nonneg

  4785	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-two-pow-rpow
  4786	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.two_pow_rpow
  4787	  kind: theorem
  4788	  summary: "For n in N and real alpha: (2^n)^alpha = (2^alpha)^n."
  4789	  keywords: [rpow, natural-power]
  4790	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4791	  status: internal
  4792	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-le-shell-sum
  4793	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.le_shellSum
  4794	  kind: theorem
  4795	  summary: "In a seminormed group, if F <= c 0 when ||x-y|| <= 1 and F <= c(n+1) when 2^n <= ||x-y|| <= 2^(n+1), then F <= sum_j 1_{closedBall y 2^j}(x) c j (ENNReal)."
  4796	  keywords: [dyadic-shell, majorant]
  4797	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4798	  status: internal
  4799	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-lintegral-shell-sum
  4800	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.lintegral_shellSum
  4801	  kind: theorem
  4802	  summary: "In a seminormed group with OpensMeasurableSpace, for any measure nu: the lintegral of sum_j 1_{closedBall y 2^j} c j equals sum_j c j * nu(closedBall y 2^j)."
  4803	  keywords: [dyadic-shell, lower-integral]
  4804	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4805	  status: internal
  4806	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-shell-sum-le
  4807	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.shellSum_le
  4808	  kind: theorem
  4809	  summary: "On a pseudometric measurable space with open-ball growth nu(ball y r) <= ofReal(C r^alpha), for c >= 0: sum_j ofReal(c j) nu(closedBall y 2^j) <= sum_j ofReal(c j C (2^alpha)^j)."
  4810	  keywords: [dyadic-shell, growth-bound]
  4811	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FrequencyRow.lean
  4812	  status: internal
  4813	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/frequency-row-row-series-nonneg
  4814	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FrequencyRow.rowSeries_nonneg

   175	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   176	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   177	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   178	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   179	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   180	\end{equation}
   181	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   182	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   183	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   184	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   185	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   186	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   187	\end{equation}
   188	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   189	
   190	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   191	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   192	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   193	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   194	  convention
   195	  \[
   196	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   197	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   198	  \]
   199	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   200	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   201	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   202	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   203	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   204	  \end{equation}
   205	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   206	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   207	\end{hypothesis}
   208	
   209	\paragraph{Zero covariance.}
   210	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} allows $\Gamma = 0$ by design. In this case the
   211	centered Gaussian noise is $\W = 0$, and the solution with initial data
   212	$(1,0)$ is $u(t,x) = 1$. Thus $\E|u(t,x)|^p = 1$ for every $p > 0$, and
   213	all normalized logarithmic moment rates are zero. Results asserting strict
   214	positivity of covariance-dependent quantities impose $\Gamma \ne 0$ locally.
   215	
   216	Throughout we write
   217	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   218	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   219	\end{equation}
   220	
   221	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   222	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   223	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   224	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   225	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   226	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   227	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   228	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   229	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   230	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   231	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   232	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   233	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   234	stochastic interpretations or temporal covariances and do not supply this
   235	identification by substitution.

    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha

    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}

   141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a
   145	    = \int_0^T\int_0^T f(t)g(s)|t-s|^{-a}\ud t\ud s
   146	  \]
   147	  is positive semidefinite on real compact smooth tests. Its null-quotient
   148	  completion $H_a$ is separable. The inclusion of tests extends continuously
   149	  from $L^2(0,T)$, with
   150	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-time-schur}
   151	    \|f\|_a^2 \le \frac{2T^{1-a}}{1-a}\|f\|_2^2.
   152	  \end{equation}
   153	  In its complexification the norm is given by the same double integral with
   154	  $f(t)\overline{f(s)}$. In particular, bounded measurable amplitudes on a
   155	  subinterval, extended by zero, belong to this completion.
   156	\end{lemma}

   159	  Write $\Gamma_E$ for Euler's Gamma function. Away from the null diagonal,
   160	  \[
   161	    |t-s|^{-a} = \frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty
   162	    \lambda^{a-1}e^{-\lambda|t-s|}\ud\lambda.
   163	  \]

   165	  \[
   166	    e^{-\lambda|t-s|}
   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.
   169	  \]

   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the
   172	  kernel row integral is at most $2T^{1-a}/(1-a)$. The same bound and $2|xy| \le
   173	  |x|^2+|y|^2$ prove~\eqref{E:masked-time-schur}. A countable $L^2$-dense family
   174	  of compact smooth tests is consequently dense in $H_a$, proving separability.
   175	  The complex quadratic form is the sum of those of the real and imaginary
   176	  parts, since symmetry cancels the imaginary cross term. Thus, the same bound
   177	  holds after complexification. Smooth density in $L^2$, together with the Schur
   178	  bound on the absolute bilinear form, extends the inclusion and the integral
   179	  identity to $L^2$. This includes the stated interval amplitudes. This proves
   180	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.

   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}

   379	  Define $c_r(t) = \cos(rt)$ and
   380	  \[
   381	    b_r(t) = \langle r\rangle\frac{\sin(rt)}r\quad(r > 0),
   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]

   387	    \le C_1(a)(1+T)^4h^{2-a}\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   388	    \qquad C_1(a) = 4\cdot3^{1-a}C_0(a).

   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
